payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does comparison with the source show an added frog placement that constitutes progress toward putting a frog inside this toilet bowl?
node.criteria: Pass if source comparison establishes a newly added frog inside the bowl, or a visibly incomplete placement into the bowl such as a frog straddling the rim with part of its body extending into the interior. Describe whether the observed placement appears inside or incomplete, without awarding completion. Fail if comparison is sufficiently clear and shows no such requested progress. A frog solely on the lid, tank, floor, or outside the opening is not requested progress. Unknown if comparison, frog identity, or the relevant spatial relation cannot be assessed reliably; apparent proximity alone does not establish partial progress.
node.binding: Use s1 as candidate-identification context, then independently compare the source and edited images. Ground progress in a visible change toward the requested bowl-interior placement, not merely the addition of frogs elsewhere. Record the spatial evidence supporting progress or its absence.

Preserve the ordered evidence roles: use s1 to identify a candidate, s2 to compare source and edit for requested progress, and s3 to assess whether that candidate is actually inside the bowl; do not count dependent observations as independent corroboration. Make the completion criterion distinguish a completed placement from visible but incomplete progress, and reserve unknown for unresolved or conflicting evidence. The five identical high-confidence “yes” outcomes despite a partial reference suggest a systematic criterion/binding mismatch, not a transport or dependency failure; investigate that mismatch rather than lowering confidence or treating repetition as proof.

Treat s2’s source comparison as the progress evidence and do not let s3’s pass, or repeated dependent descriptions of the same frog, imply that all requested changes are complete. Preserve the ordered s1→s2→s3 evidence roles and use unknown only for genuinely unresolved geometry. The repeated high-confidence yes outcomes point to a criterion/binding mismatch, not a transport or dependency failure; investigate that mismatch rather than lowering confidence or forcing a label from the reference.
